Theme

School & learning · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

problem noun

to be solved

also maths problem, solve a problem

classical

Sen. Ep. 48.11: quaestiōnem solvere (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 364

quaestiō, quaestiōnis f.

noun, third declension

a problem to be solved, a question

Solve a problem: quaestiōnem solvere (Sen., Quint.).

Other words

  • problēma, problēmatis n. — a problem set for solving, a puzzle

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Suet. Gram. 4 (Lewis & Short); Gell. 19.4.1 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 364: problēma, a problem in mathematics

    The Greek word, in Suetonius and Gellius (Lewis & Short: post-Augustan).

Examples

  • Hanc quaestiōnem sōlus solvistī?

    Did you solve this problem by yourself?composed

See also problem, riddle, question, solution.

SourcesLewis & Short: quaestio · Lewis & Short: problema

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
